source_text: Non potest dici morbus, sine quo non est connubium: quia potest esse connubium praeter peccatum; morbus autem ab Apostolo peccatum dicitur Si non sunt nuptiae sine libidine, et generaliter a vobis libido damnatur, damnatis et nuptias
pass_a_gloss: Not is-able dici morbus, without whither not is connubium: because is-able to-be connubium except sin; morbus however from Apostolo sin is-said if not are marriages without by-lust, and generally from to-you lust condemns, condemns and marriages.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good

pass_b_english: If there is no marriage without desire, and you condemn desire in general, you condemn marriage too.
That without which marriage does not exist cannot be called a disease. Marriage can exist apart from sin; but the apostle calls disease sin.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
